result.markdown:
# DIY guide: Filing a UK company confirmation statement and dormant accounts

Yes — you can generally do both yourself without paying an accountant or company formation agency.

For a straightforward UK private limited company that has not traded and has remained dormant, the annual compliance process is relatively simple.

There are two separate obligations\:

1. **Confirmation statement (CS01)** – confirms that your company's details at Companies House are correct.
2. **Dormant company accounts (AA02)** – reports that the company has had no significant accounting transactions during the financial year.

You must file both, even if the company has never traded or has no income, expenses or bank activity. [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/filing-your-companys-confirmation-statement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/dormant-company/dormant-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 1\. What will it cost DIY?

Annual Companies House filing fees

# £50

Confirmation statement online

---

Dormant accounts filing (£0)

---

**Total DIY annual cost** **£50**

The £50 confirmation statement fee is payable once per 12-month payment period. Dormant accounts have no Companies House filing fee.

By comparison, an agency might charge you £100–£300 or more in service fees on top of statutory filing fees.

Official fee information: [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/filing-your-companys-confirmation-statement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/dormant-company/dormant-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/companies-house-fees/companies-house-fees?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/confirmation-statement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 2\. How to file your confirmation statement (CS01)

(DIY – straightforward)

**Step 1 – Find your company**

Go to the official Companies House register\:

[Search Companies House](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/)

Enter your company name or company registration number.

Check\:

- Registered office address
- Directors
- Shareholders
- People with Significant Control (PSC)
- SIC business activity code
- Confirmation statement date
- Filing deadline

**Step 2 – Check whether anything has changed**

If everything is correct, you can proceed with the confirmation statement.

If something is incorrect, update the relevant company information first. For example, director changes, registered office changes and PSC changes generally need separate filings.

**Step 3 – Check identity verification**

This is particularly important under the newer Companies House rules.

Directors must verify their identity and provide their Companies House personal code when required for the confirmation statement. PSCs also have identity verification obligations.

[Official identity verification instructions](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/verifying-your-identity-for-companies-house)

**Step 4 – File online**

Use the official service\:

[File your confirmation statement](https://www.gov.uk/file-your-confirmation-statement-with-companies-house)

You will generally need\:

- Company number
- Companies House authentication code
- Companies House account
- Directors' personal codes
- Debit or credit card for the £50 fee

If your company is eligible for the simplified service, it can take approximately 15 minutes.

Some companies need to use the WebFiling service instead, particularly where their shareholder or officer structure does not meet the simplified service criteria. [find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/confirmation-statement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/filing-your-companys-confirmation-statement?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 3\. How to file dormant company accounts (AA02)

(DIY – no filing fee)

First, establish whether your company actually qualifies as dormant.

For Companies House purposes, a company is dormant if it has had no significant accounting transactions during its financial year.

Examples of transactions that do not count as significant include\:

- Companies House filing fees.
- Penalties for late filing.
- Initial subscriber share payments when the company was incorporated.

Be careful: a company can be dormant for Corporation Tax but not necessarily dormant for Companies House purposes. [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/dormant-company/dormant-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts/life-of-a-company-part-1-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/file-your-dormant-accounts-aa02?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/late-filing-penalties-from-companies-house/late-filing-penalties?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Step 1 – Access the dormant accounts service**

[File dormant accounts online – Companies House](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/guides/accounts/chooser/dormant)

**Step 2 – Log in**

You need\:

- Companies House WebFiling email address
- Password
- Company authentication code

If you don't have an authentication code, you can request one. Companies House normally posts it to the registered office, allowing up to five days for delivery. [find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/guides/accounts/chooser/dormant?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Step 3 – Complete the dormant accounts**

Follow the online questions and check the information carefully.

The filing generally requires\:

- Company name and registration number
- Accounting period end date
- Balance sheet information
- Required dormant company declarations

For a company that has never traded and qualifies for the simplified procedure, AA02 is relevant.

**Important distinction\:** The paper AA02 form is specifically intended for companies that have never traded, with no transactions other than the issue of subscriber shares. If your company previously traded and subsequently became dormant, you need properly prepared dormant accounts rather than relying on that simplified paper form. [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/dormant-company/dormant-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts/life-of-a-company-part-1-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/file-your-dormant-accounts-aa02?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/late-filing-penalties-from-companies-house/late-filing-penalties?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. Know your deadlines

For an ordinary private limited company\:

| Filing | Deadline |
|--------|--------|
| Confirmation statement | At least once every 12 months, with up to 14 days after the review period |
| Annual accounts | 9 months after financial year-end |


For example, if your financial year ends on 31 March, your accounts normally need to reach Companies House by 31 December.

Late accounts penalties for private companies are\:

| How late? | Penalty |
|--------|--------|
| Up to 1 month | £150 |
| 1–3 months | £375 |
| 3–6 months | £750 |
| Over 6 months | £1,500 |


These penalties double if accounts are late in two consecutive financial years. [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts/life-of-a-company-part-1-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/late-filing-penalties-from-companies-house/late-filing-penalties?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 5\. Don't forget HMRC – a separate obligation

This is where some DIY company owners make mistakes.

Companies House and HMRC are two different organisations.

Even if your company is dormant at Companies House, you should check its Corporation Tax status separately.

If HMRC has issued a notice to deliver a Company Tax Return (CT600), you generally need to submit it unless HMRC confirms that you do not need to.

If HMRC has formally treated the company as dormant for Corporation Tax, you may not need to submit annual CT600 returns while that status continues.

You can check and manage this through\:

[HMRC Corporation Tax services](https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax)

Also note an important 2026 change: the old joint online service for filing company accounts and Corporation Tax returns closed on 31 March 2026. You can still use the separate Companies House accounts services, but HMRC tax returns need an appropriate separate filing route. [www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company?ctype=5&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/dormant-company/dormant-for-companies-house?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 6\. Important 2026 changes to be aware of

Companies House is introducing stronger identity verification requirements.

Also, its accounts filing arrangements are changing towards commercial software-only filing in future.

However, the current guidance still provides online filing options, including the dormant accounts service.

Official guidance\:

- [Companies House online filing](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/filing-your-companies-house-information-online)
- [Companies House accounts filing changes](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/filing-your-companies-house-accounts)

## 7\. My recommended DIY annual checklist

## 8\. I can help you do the actual filings yourself

If you give me a little information about your company, I can guide you through the exact process, including which accounts filing route to use.

**Three questions\:**

1. Is your company a UK private limited company (Ltd)?
2. Has it been dormant since incorporation, or did it previously trade and subsequently become dormant?
3. Is it just one director and one shareholder, or are there multiple directors/shareholders?

If you also provide the company's accounting year-end month, I can help establish the filing deadlines.

**My objective would be to help you complete both Companies House filings for the statutory £50 fee, without paying an agency to do the paperwork.**
